name: Sunday Times mephisto crossword No 3,000
setter: Tim Moorey, Paul McKenna and Don Manley

solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maestro playing out of his skin is a star

indicators.note: a word stripped of its skin loses its outermost letters at each end, leaving only the inside
playing suggests the letters are performed afresh, in a new order

blocks.note: the conductor's word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A conductor performing beyond himself is hailed as a star turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of his skin' sounds like an idiom for frenzied excitement; here it peels the outer letters off the maestro.
explanation.definitionFit: Aster comes from the Greek word for a star, and Chambers gives it as a star-shaped figure as well as the flower.

clue.text: A beard must scrape

indicators.note: must is the frenzied state of a male elephant in rut, so these letters run wild

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man with a beard has to shave it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Must' reads as an auxiliary verb; in Chambers it is also musth, an elephant's frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to rub or scrape away a surface by friction.

clue.text: Second fast bowler may be someone out of this world

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
in cricket a paceman is a fast bowler

explanation.surface: A second fast bowler in the cricket team might seem out of this world.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a paceman bowls fast rather than spin.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceman is an astronaut, literally someone gone beyond this world.

clue.text: So much the worse — National Trust destroyed old arras?

indicators.note: the letters for the Trust are destroyed, so they vanish from the phrase

blocks.note: tant pis is French for so much the worse
NT abbreviates National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A shrug at the National Trust wrecking an antique tapestry.
explanation.walkthrough: The NT removed is the N and T in the middle of tant pis. The question mark flags that a tapis is an old word for a hanging or carpet, of which an arras is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapis is an obsolete term for tapestry or a table carpet, the material of an arras hanging.

clue.text: Medicine futile ultimately with this person twitching

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: the last letter
the setter refers to themself
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: The medicine proves useless in the end, leaving me twitching.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a medicine that induces vomiting.

clue.text: Plants in magic pot vary unexpectedly, five dying

indicators.note: dying means passing away, so the letter for five disappears from the fodder
unexpectedly suggests things turn out otherwise, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder letters
Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Plants grown in a magic pot behave unpredictably, and five of them die.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptogamia is the old Linnaean class of plants without flowers or seeds, such as ferns, mosses and fungi.

clue.text: Galley recipe one found in plane?

definitions.note: defines TRIREME; the grid entry drops its M (1,000), as the preamble requires

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so the earlier pieces go inside the tree

blocks.note: a plane is a kind of tree
R is the abbreviation for recipe (take), from prescriptions
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A ship's-kitchen recipe turns up on an aeroplane, the question mark admitting the absurdity.
explanation.walkthrough: A special clue: the preamble says one clue per row has wordplay and entry both short of Roman numerals. The definition gives TRIREME, the wordplay only TRIREE, so the missing M (1,000) counts towards the 3,000 total.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme is an ancient war galley with three banks of oars.

clue.text: Escaper breaking free with 'eavy load

indicators.note: breaking means smashing apart, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a heavy load is huge; the dropped h of 'eavy shows it is dropped here too

explanation.surface: A prisoner breaks out carrying a heavy load, in Cockney.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'eavy imitates Cockney speech, which drops initial h's, so the large load loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is someone who has fled, escaping persecution or danger.

clue.text: Early English architect's design initially coming out of the blue

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is taken
coming out of means leaving, so that letter is removed from the colour

blocks.note: indigo is a deep shade of blue
the first letter

explanation.surface: An early architect's plan arrives out of the blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of the blue' looks like the idiom for unexpectedly; here it splits so a letter comes out of a shade of blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Inigo Jones was the seventeenth-century English architect who brought Palladian style to England.

clue.text: US city's Irish painter

blocks.note: Reno is a city in Nevada
IR is an abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: An Irish painter based in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Earl being given vote

blocks.note: esse is Latin for being, existence
a vote is marked with a cross on the ballot paper

explanation.surface: A nobleman is given the vote.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Essex is a famous title, held by Elizabeth I's favourite Robert Devereux.

clue.text: Seen to need treatment, inside leg being raw

definitions.note: defines CRUDENESS; the grid entry drops its D (500)

indicators.note: letters that need treatment are to be worked on and rearranged
inside places the reworked letters within the word for a leg

blocks.note: crus is the anatomical term for the leg between knee and ankle
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor's note: the inside leg measurement is raw and must be seen to.
explanation.walkthrough: A special clue: the definition gives CRUDENESS but the wordplay builds it without the D (500), which the grid also leaves out.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudeness is the condition of being unrefined or unprocessed, the state of something raw.

clue.text: European dismissal in turn sadly not stopping

indicators.note: in places the first pieces within the reworked letters
sadly means things have gone badly, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
E is the abbreviation for European
to get the mitten was to be rejected as a suitor, so a mitten is a dismissal

explanation.surface: A European is sent packing, which unhappily goes on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Unremittent means unremitting, continuing without any let-up or pause.

clue.text: Fabric covering a penetrating beam

definitions.note: defines DRAPERY; the grid entry drops its D (500)

indicators.note: something penetrating another goes into it, so this word sits inside the beam

blocks.note: a beam of light is a ray
as in 'ten pounds a head', a means per

explanation.surface: A cloth cover pierced by a beam of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like a mere article, but it stands for PER. A special clue: the definition is DRAPERY, and the D (500) is missing from wordplay and grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Drapery is cloth hung in folds, a fabric covering for windows or walls.

clue.text: Close search, mostly during breaks

indicators.note: mostly means not all of the word, so its last letter is dropped
a word that breaks another splits it open and sits between its parts

blocks.note: to fish for something is to search for it
in, as in 'in the night', means during

explanation.surface: A search wound up, mostly carried on during the breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Finis is the Latin word printed at the end of a book, meaning the close or conclusion.

clue.text: Name behind Australian rock

definitions.note: defines DACITE; the grid entry drops its D (500)

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the word for name is placed second, after the abbreviation

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for Australian
to cite is to name, as a source or witness

explanation.surface: A name lurking behind Australia's famous rock, Uluru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' puts CITE after A. A special clue: the rock is DACITE and the D (500) is absent from wordplay and grid; crossings in the row rule out CALCITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dacite is a volcanic igneous rock, named after Dacia, the old name for the region of Romania.

clue.text: Stall wrapping bargain for wrinkly

indicators.note: wrapping means enclosing, so the first word folds around the second

blocks.note: a stall is a decoy or pretext to delay, a ruse
a go is a bargain or deal, as in 'it's a go'

explanation.surface: A market stall gift-wraps a bargain for an elderly shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stall' suggests a market booth; it means a delaying trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugose is a botanical and zoological word for wrinkled or ridged, as a leaf surface can be.

clue.text: Dry Asian who's pukka scoffed

definitions.note: defines DESICCATE; the grid entry drops both its Cs (200)

blocks.note: desi, from Hindi for local or genuine, is a person of South Asian origin
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A dry remark about a genuine Asian who mocked something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' looks like mocked, but means ate. A special clue: the definition is DESICCATE and both Cs (200) are missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To desiccate is to remove moisture, to dry thoroughly.

clue.text: Exaggerate point, possibly involving silly lie?

indicators.note: possibly hints the letters could be arranged another way
silly suggests letters acting foolishly, out of their order
involving means wrapping up, so one set of letters encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Is overstating a point a matter of telling silly lies?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue nearly reads as its own definition: exaggerating may well involve a silly lie.
explanation.definitionFit: To pile it on is an idiom meaning to overstate or exaggerate.

clue.text: Mike with capital cut suffering with respect to gauging gear

definitions.note: defines MICROMETRICAL; the grid entry drops its C (100) and L (50)

indicators.note: a word that is cut loses its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a mike or mic is a microphone
the Italian capital
a trial is an ordeal or suffering

explanation.surface: Mike's capital was slashed, and he suffers over the measuring equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: A special clue: the definition is MICROMETRICAL, and its C (100) and L (50) are missing from wordplay and grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Micrometrical describes measurement with a micrometer, an instrument for gauging tiny distances.

clue.text: What's needed is missing return

indicators.note: missing means absent, so that little word goes from the longer one

blocks.note: a requisite is something needed
taken as written

explanation.surface: The required item is lost and must be sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like a verb but is the pair of letters lifted out.
explanation.definitionFit: To requite is to repay or return, as kindness or a wrong.

clue.text: Hear angelic playing here, perhaps

definitions.note: defines CARNEGIE HALL; the grid entry drops its final L (50)

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are performed in a different arrangement

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to hear heavenly music in a concert venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition. A special clue: the hall is CARNEGIE HALL, but the anagram only supplies one L, so the second L (50) is absent from the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnegie Hall is the famous New York concert venue, where one may well hear angelic playing.

clue.text: Huckleberry Finn, say, is for foot — it's uplifting

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer, a thing that lifts

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one pair stands where the other was

blocks.note: Huck Finn travelled the Mississippi on a raft, so he is a rafter
taken as written
FT is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: Huck Finn's adventures stand in for footwork, and the story is uplifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Huck Finn as an example of a rafter, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A raiser is anything that raises or lifts, so it is literally uplifting.

clue.text: Heart of this madness is cost of borrowing for Kiwi

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: the middle two letters
rage is a fit of madness

explanation.surface: At the heart of it, crazy New Zealand loan charges.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiwi is the nickname for a New Zealander, signalling a New Zealand word.
explanation.definitionFit: In New Zealand hirage is the charge for hiring something, a cost of borrowing it.

clue.text: Retired Jew by nature not cold

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: the essence of a thing is its nature
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A Jewish pensioner who is warm by nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like 'stopped working'; it means withdrawn from the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect living apart in communities, such as at Qumran.

clue.text: Floor that is small part of theatre

blocks.note: FL is an abbreviation for floor
i.e. is Latin id est, that is
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A floor, that is a small area of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The flies are the space above a theatre stage where scenery is hung.

clue.text: Relative is careless about what winds up some

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for careless goes round the extra letter
what winds up a word is what comes at its end, its last letter

blocks.note: nice in an old sense means wanton or careless
the last letter

explanation.surface: Some relative is being careless about family matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a relative, the daughter of one's brother or sister.

clue.text: Seeing that twinkling within parents of dependent young

definitions.note: defines ALTRICES; the grid entry drops its L (50)

indicators.note: within places the second idea inside the phrase for seeing that

blocks.note: as means seeing that, since
in a twinkling means in a trice, an instant

explanation.surface: Since there is a twinkle within the parents of needy youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: A special clue: the definition is ALTRICES, and the L (50) is missing from wordplay and grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Altrices are birds whose chicks hatch helpless and must be fed in the nest, unlike precocial species.

clue.text: College fell for fad

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for college
to fell a building is to raze it

explanation.surface: A college took a tumble over a passing fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' reads as fell down; it is the verb meaning knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze is a short-lived enthusiasm, a fashion or fad.

clue.text: Teuchter's topper thrice stuck by touch of industrial detergent

definitions.note: defines LIXIVIUM; the grid entry drops its X (10) and V (5)

indicators.note: a touch is just a little, so only the opening letter of the following word is used, here thrice over
the Scotsman's topper is stuck through by the letters, which go inside it

blocks.note: a Teuchter is a Highlander; lum is Scots for chimney, and a lum hat is a top hat
the first letter
thrice means that letter appears three times, so two more copies

explanation.surface: A Highlander's top hat gets three dabs of industrial cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: A special clue: the definition is LIXIVIUM, and its X (10) and V (5) are missing from wordplay and grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lixivium is lye, an alkaline solution leached from ashes and used as a detergent.

clue.text: Lace designer of Victorian era losing money

indicators.note: losing means giving something up, so a letter is taken off the designer's name

blocks.note: William Morris, the Victorian designer of wallpapers and textiles
M is an abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: A Victorian lace designer falls on hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is a gold or silver lace or braid once used to trim clothing.

clue.text: Whale coming to island — one has crossed the Pacific

blocks.note: IS is an abbreviation for island
the sei is a species of rorqual whale

explanation.surface: A whale reaches an island after a long Pacific voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming to' means arriving at, so the whale follows the island in the answer. Issei is a Japanese word, literally 'first generation'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Issei is a first-generation Japanese emigrant to North America, someone who made the Pacific crossing.

clue.text: Remove soil from disgusting Siamese cat! (Miss terribly put off)

definitions.note: defines EXCAVATE; the grid entry drops its X (10) and V (5)

indicators.note: put off means sent away, so those letters are taken out of the fodder
disgusting suggests something turned and spoilt, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the ten letters of the fodder
these letters, in jumbled order as terribly signals, come out of the fodder

explanation.surface: Clean the soil off that revolting Siamese cat, poor Miss is appalled!
explanation.walkthrough: A special clue: the definition is EXCAVATE, and its X (10) and V (5) are missing from wordplay and grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To excavate is to dig out and remove earth from a site.

clue.text: Eager worker going after record, a shocking experience

definitions.note: defines EXPECTANT; the grid entry drops its X (10)

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, treatment by electric shock
the worker ant

explanation.surface: A keen employee follows a record that proved an electrifying experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The worker goes after both record and shock treatment. A special clue: the definition is EXPECTANT, and the X (10) is missing from wordplay and grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Expectant means eagerly awaiting something, keyed up in anticipation.

clue.text: Monastic group that's observed outside part of church?

indicators.note: outside means the word for observed goes around the order's letters

blocks.note: observed means seen
CR is the Community of the Resurrection, an Anglican religious order

explanation.surface: A monastic community is watched outside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a rood screen is one part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen, such as a rood screen, divides the chancel from the nave in many churches.

clue.text: Chemical explosive with forcefulness, not half!

definitions.note: defines HEXENE; the grid entry drops its X (10)

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word survives, its first three letters

blocks.note: HE stands for high explosive
energy is forcefulness or vigour

explanation.surface: A chemical explosive with real force, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' reads as a British exclamation meaning very much so. A special clue: the definition is HEXENE, and the X (10) is missing from wordplay and grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Hexene is a hydrocarbon, an alkene with six carbon atoms, used in making polyethylene.
